source_notes.label: Sulfur ratio selects oxide, mixed phase or disulfide
source_notes.summary: Under the reported 300 °C, 12 h solvothermal conditions, Table 1 and Figure 1 assign MoO2 to the no-sulfur feed, MoO2 + MoS2 to MoO3:S = 1:1, and MoS2 to 1:2 and 1:3. The typical 1:2 feed contains 0.576 g (4 mmol) MoO3 and 8 mmol sulfur; the printed sulfur number 0.256 lacks a mass unit. Other ratios do not establish their own absolute precursor charges.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–3, Preparation, Figure 1 and Table 1

source_notes.label: Phase identification and composition remain distinct
source_notes.summary: The two sulfur-rich products are indexed as 2H-MoS2, space group P63/mmc (194), with (002), (100), (103) and (110) reflections. Chemical analysis reports MoS1.99 for 1:2 and MoS2.02 for 1:3. These are chemical-analysis compositions, not refined site occupancies or a measure of interfacial geometry.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, XRD and chemical-analysis discussion

source_notes.label: Study-wide dimensions are not two separately measured batches
source_notes.summary: The paper reports refined a = 3.16 Å and c = 12.40 Å and describes thin platelets around 100 nm. Figure 2b is an individual particle about 200 nm across. The text does not uniquely map those observations to ratio c or d; the individual particle is not a second population mean. Reference-card values a0 = 3.1616 Å and c0 = 12.2985 Å are literature comparison data, not new measurements.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, XRD refinement paragraph and Figure 2

source_notes.label: IR supports the authors’ no-intercalation interpretation
source_notes.summary: The prose assigns an IR band at 382 cm⁻¹; Figure 3 labels 382.8. The reported absence of bands from 500 to 4000 cm⁻¹ is interpreted by the authors as no guest pyridine between the MoS2 layers. This is their spectral interpretation, not a quantitative limit on every possible impurity. The analyzed ratio-specific batch is not identified.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and IR discussion

source_notes.label: The proposed MoO2 intermediate
source_notes.summary: The authors propose reduction of MoO3 to MoO2 by hydrazine, followed by sulfidation to MoS2. Adding sufficient sulfur to the mixed 1:1 product and replacing MoO3 with MoO2 are reported to yield MoS2, but those supporting tests lack separate charge and schedule details. Equations 1 and 2 are proposed reaction steps, not measured transient concentrations.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Mechanistic discussion and equations 1–2

source_notes.label: Temperature limits and solvent role
source_notes.summary: Below 250 °C the reaction requires a long time; above 350 °C pyridine may decompose without greatly improving MoS2 crystallinity. Exact temperature series and durations are not supplied. The authors choose 300 °C for 12 h and describe pyridine as heat-stable at the chosen conditions, sulfur-solubilizing and miscible with hydrazine. Lubrication suitability is a proposed application; no functional performance test is reported.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–4, Temperature discussion and conclusion
